role: You are a visual educator, motion designer, and Remotion developer.
task: Build a 60-second, 9:16 DataEntropy explainer animation that shows beginners what a SQL window function is: it calculates across a set of related rows, the window, while every row stays its own row. Show OVER, PARTITION BY and ORDER BY inside the window. Carry one example through the whole video: Farid, a sales manager, wants each sale shown beside its team total. Deliver complete, editable Remotion code and a rendered MP4.

reference.project: diffusion-video (60-second template) and sql-select-video (the series pilot: table cards, query card, typing, check marks)
take_inspiration_from: Continuous transformations instead of slide changes
Objects moving in response to a question
Labels appearing exactly when their meaning becomes clear
A viewer feeling as though they are discovering the mechanism
reference.originality: Create original artwork, colors, typography, and compositions.

video.audience: Beginners: students and early-career professionals who want practical data skills. Simple, friendly language; every necessary term is explained in plain words in the same scene.
video.structure: The brand guideline's 30-second structure scaled to 60 seconds: hook, problem, explanation, outcome, call to action in the last 6 seconds. 11 scenes, each about 4-6 seconds.
video.style: Clean, minimal vector line-art motion graphics on a white (#FFFFFF) background with off-white (#F8F7FC) content cards and generous whitespace. Deep navy (#172554) for headlines, labels, table outlines and cell text; brand violet (#6D4AFF) for SQL keywords, the active table part, check marks and arrows; electric purple (#8B5CF6) for motion accents; soft lavender (#C4B5FD) only as filled bands, pills or glows placed behind navy text or a darker outline. Tables are white rounded cards with a bold 5px outline, a navy name tab and bold navy text. Text that is not picked turns pale gray (#D6D2E0) and is never the focus. Every line, arrow, connector and outline is a bold 4-6px stroke with rounded endpoints in deep navy, brand violet or electric purple. Rounded corners 8-20px, soft low-opacity violet-tinted shadows. No dark backgrounds, no red, orange or neon colors. At most three focal points per scene.
video.typography: Inter (fallback Arial, sans-serif). Headlines weight 700, at least 54px, deep navy, left-aligned at the top of the safe area, maximum two lines and 12 words, with one or two key words in brand violet. Table text and labels at least 32px on screen, deep navy. SQL code in JetBrains Mono, at least 32px on screen.
video.subtitles: Enabled in the lower-middle safe area. Inter SemiBold white (#FFFFFF) text inside a solid rounded deep navy (#172554, 88% opacity) box; maximum 2 lines and 7 words per line; word-group reveal synchronized with the voiceover; key words in soft lavender (#C4B5FD).
video.safe_area: Top 10%, bottom 18%, left 7%, right 7%. Headlines, subtitles, logo and CTA stay inside x 76-1004px and y 192-1574px. Headline zone y 192-400; world content y 400-1390; subtitle bar bottom edge at y 1560.
video.voiceover: Voice en-US-AvaNeural (the diffusion explainer's voice), per-line pace fitted with tools/fit_vo_pace.py. 135-155 words per minute while speaking. Few commas, because each comma adds a pause.
video.mobile_readability: Use large text, short labels, and generous spacing. Keep essential content inside platform-safe margins.

central_visual.description: TOP: the table 'sales' (rep, region, amount) with one extra column for the window function's result, a white card with a bold 5px deep navy outline. BELOW: the query card with a bold 5px navy outline.
central_visual.interaction_effect: The window is a bold brand-violet outline around the rows a calculation can see: all rows for an empty OVER, one window per team for PARTITION BY, and a window that grows row by row for ORDER BY. The last column's values change with it.
central_visual.camera: One continuous space: close on the table, then out to the table and the query card.

timeline.visual: A white table card named 'sales' with a bold 5px deep navy outline draws itself: columns rep, region and amount, five rows of bold navy text, and one more column with an empty header and a bold brand-violet question mark in it. Headline with 'beside' in brand violet.
timeline.on_screen_text: Each sale beside its team total?
timeline.voiceover: Farid wants every sale next to its team total. On the same row.

timeline.visual: Under the table a small result card with a bold 5px navy outline and the tab 'GROUP BY' draws itself with two rows, East 800 and West 700, and a white chip with a bold navy outline reads '5 rows became 2'. Headline: 'squeezes' in brand violet.
timeline.on_screen_text: GROUP BY squeezes the rows away
timeline.voiceover: GROUP BY gives the totals. But it squeezes five rows into two.

timeline.visual: The small result card fades away. In the sales table the header of the last column turns brand violet with the white word 'total', and a bold 5px brand-violet outline draws itself around that column, still empty, beside all five rows. Headline: 'window function' in brand violet.
timeline.on_screen_text: A window function keeps every row
timeline.voiceover: A window function adds up too. But it keeps every row.

timeline.visual: Below, a white query card with a bold 5px navy outline draws itself and types four lines: SELECT rep, amount, then SUM(amount) OVER with an open bracket, a closing bracket, and FROM sales, with the keywords in bold brand violet. A bold 5px brand-violet outline, the window, draws itself around all five rows, and every row's total reads 1,500. Headline: 'OVER' in brand violet.
timeline.voiceover: OVER means: look through a window at other rows. Here, all of them.

timeline.visual: Inside the brackets of the query 'PARTITION BY region' slides in. The single window fades and two bold 5px brand-violet windows draw themselves, one around the two East rows and one around the three West rows. The totals slide to 800 for the East rows and 700 for the West rows. Headline: 'PARTITION BY' in brand violet.
timeline.on_screen_text: PARTITION BY: one window per team
timeline.voiceover: PARTITION BY region makes one window for each team.

timeline.visual: A white chip with a bold brand-violet outline and navy text '5 rows in, 5 rows out' is revealed above the table, and soft lavender bands spread behind the navy totals. Headline: 'five rows out' in brand violet.
timeline.on_screen_text: Five rows in, five rows out
timeline.voiceover: Each row gets its team's total and stays its own row.

timeline.visual: The line inside the brackets changes to 'ORDER BY amount'. The two windows fade, the totals clear, and the rows slide past each other until the amounts run from 100 at the top to 500 at the bottom. A bold 5px brand-violet window appears around the first row only and its total reads 100. Headline: 'running total' in brand violet.
timeline.on_screen_text: ORDER BY inside: a running total
timeline.voiceover: Put ORDER BY inside the window and the sum becomes a running total.

timeline.visual: The brand-violet window stretches down one row at a time, and each time the newly included row gets its total: 300, 600, 1,000 and 1,500. Headline: 'row by row' in brand violet.
timeline.on_screen_text: The window grows row by row
timeline.voiceover: The window grows one row at a time, down to the current row.

timeline.visual: In the query SUM(amount) slides out and RANK() slides in. The header of the last column changes from 'total' to 'rank' and the totals slide out as the bold navy ranks 1 to 5 slide in. Headline: 'other functions' in brand violet.
timeline.voiceover: Swap SUM for RANK and the same window gives each sale a rank.

timeline.visual: A bold 5px brand-violet outline draws itself around the last column of the table, next to the five untouched rows. Headline: 'side by side' in brand violet.
timeline.on_screen_text: Totals and detail side by side
timeline.voiceover: Totals and detail, side by side. That is a window function.

timeline.visual: The tables and the query card fade away. The DataEntropy logo's four bars grow upward left to right in brand violet, the wordmark is revealed, and a soft violet glow settles. The tagline is revealed, then one brand-violet CTA button with a white animated arrow: 'Follow DataEntropy'. Hold the final composition for at least two seconds.
timeline.voiceover: Follow DataEntropy for more SQL explained simply.

animation_rules: VISIBILITY ON WHITE: every line, arrow, connector, outline and text must be clearly visible on the white background. Draw them as bold strokes of at least 4px in deep navy (#172554), brand violet (#6D4AFF) or electric purple (#8B5CF6). Use soft lavender (#C4B5FD) only for filled bands, pills or glows behind navy text, never for lines, small dots or text.
No abrupt slide cuts; every scene transforms naturally into the next in one continuous space with a camera.
Animate concepts, not decorative particles. Every animation has a job.
One example carries the whole video. The tables keep their identity and position from scene to scene.

SQL on screen is one short query in a monospace face, typed clause by clause, with keywords in brand violet. Use only syntax that works the same in PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite and SQL Server; leave dialect-specific syntax such as LIMIT or TOP off screen.
Rows have no built-in order. Do not say or imply that an answer comes back in table order unless the query has ORDER BY.
All names, cities and amounts are invented illustrative examples.
Explain every necessary term in plain words in the same scene it appears.
Synchronize each label and highlight with its voiceover phrase.
Use deterministic frame-based animation so any frame renders correctly when scrubbing the timeline.
Use the brand easing cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); no rapid flashing, glitch effects or excessive bouncing.
Nothing rises or scales as it appears: card outlines draw themselves and fill in, rows and chips are wiped in from the left.
A window function never removes or merges rows: five rows go in and five come out in every scene after GROUP BY is set aside.

An empty OVER looks at all rows; PARTITION BY makes one window per group; ORDER BY inside OVER makes the window run from the first row to the current row, which is why the sum becomes a running total.
Amounts are all different, so the running total has no ties to explain.
Window functions need MySQL 8.0 or later and SQLite 3.25 or later; do not name versions on screen.

implementation.graphics: Original SVG and code-generated shapes; no stock footage or paid assets

deliverables: Remotion preview and MP4 render commands
Brief explanation of where to edit text, colors, and timing
quality_check: Render and inspect a still at the key moment of every scene. Fix clipping, overlaps, unreadable labels and any line or text that is hard to see on white. Confirm every value in the last column: 1,500 for all rows, then 800 and 700 by team, then the running totals 100, 300, 600, 1,000, 1,500, then ranks 1 to 5.
